title: Pricing Day and The Grumpy Hiker
goal: I can skip-count by 5s and 10s to find price totals, and I can compare two characters' points of view.

card.desc: Theo thinks a grumpy hiker is rude, but Mia spots clues he missed. You compare their two points of view and use clues to infer. Then you make price tags for Grandpa's shelves: skip-count by 5s and 10s and multiply price × quantity = total (Pathways Week 7). No work on Friday, New Year's Day.

win: You saw the hiker through Theo's eyes and Mia's eyes, and you priced Grandpa's shelves. Happy New Year!

slides.title: Welcome Back, Ce'Line!
slides.text:
Welcome back! I hope you had a happy holiday. 🎉
Today Grandpa's trading post opens.
A grumpy hiker walks in. Is he rude, or is something else going on?
Then you help make price tags. 🏷️

notes.do: Before class: laptop open to this class lesson (code 9110). Whiteboard and 2 marker colors. 2 index cards that say THEO and MIA. 20 paper money slips cut from index cards: 10 say $5 and 10 say $10. 6 blank index cards for price tags. Her printed Packet for Lesson 7. Take her Lesson 6 Packet page 2 and look at it while she settles in.
notes.say: Welcome back! I missed you. Today has two parts: a story about a grumpy hiker, then price tags for Grandpa's shelves.
notes.ask: What was the best part of your break?
notes.listen: Any answer. Keep it to 1–2 minutes and let her talk. Glance at her Lesson 6 packet and her Pathways Week 6 scores now; fix only what takes a minute.

slides.title: Remember Weeks 1 to 6
slides.text: Five quick ones from your fall lessons.

items.q: Round 817 to the nearest hundred: ____
items.why: 817 is between 800 and 900. The tens digit is 1. 1 is less than 5, so round down to 800.
items.no: Look at the tens digit. Is it 5 or more?
items.hint: The tens digit is 1. Round down.

items.why: 8 + 4 = 12: write 2, regroup 1 ten. 8 + 8 + 1 = 17 tens: write 7, regroup 1 hundred. 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. 872.
items.no: Line up the places. Did you regroup two times?

items.q: Estimate 63 + 79. Round each number to the nearest ten, then add: ____
items.no: Round first: 63 is close to 60. 79 is close to 80.

items.q: Write 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 as multiplication: ____
items.no: Count the 7s. That is the number of groups.

items.q: The road was icy, so the bus drove slowly. What is the cause?
items.why: The ice is why the bus went slowly. It is the cause.
no: Driving slowly is what happened. That is the effect.
The sentence does not say that.

notes.do: She says each answer out loud first, then types or taps. These are skills from Weeks 1–6, so they stay fresh.
notes.listen: 800, 872, 140, 5 × 7 (7 × 5 is fine), the road was icy. If she gets 862 or 772 for 388 + 484, she lost a regrouped ten or hundred: write it in columns on the whiteboard.

slides.title: The Grumpy Hiker
slides.text: Read the story with Mr. Jonathan. Take turns, one line each.

visual.text:
It was opening day at Grandpa's trading post.
A hiker walked in. He looked around for a minute.
Then he left. He did not buy anything.
Theo felt hurt. He thought the hiker was being rude.
Mia looked closer. The hiker's boots were caked in mud. The strap on his pack was torn. His water bottle was empty.
Mia inferred that the hiker was not rude. He was exhausted (very, very tired).
Mia told Theo what she saw. Theo's hurt feelings were real. Mia's idea was probably true too.

prompts: How did Theo feel? What did he think?

notes.do: 6 minutes. Take turns reading lines aloud. Put the THEO card on the left and the MIA card on the right.
notes.say: Same hiker, same moment. But Theo and Mia saw it in two different ways.
notes.ask: Was the hiker rude? How do you know?
notes.listen: Theo thought he was rude. Mia noticed muddy boots, a torn strap and an empty water bottle, so she thought he was exhausted. Check that she knows exhausted means very, very tired. Pathways asks her to type rude and exhausted.

slides.title: Reading words
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Read the word. Then say what it means in your own words.

words.meaning: The way one person sees a moment.
words.example: From Theo's point of view, the hiker was rude.

words.meaning: A person's own way of seeing or understanding something.
Understanding and caring about how someone else feels.
words.example: Mia showed empathy for the tired hiker.

words.meaning: To explain what something means to you.
words.example: Theo and Mia interpreted the same moment in two ways.

notes.do: Flip each card. She reads the word and the meaning, then says it in her own words. Write POINT OF VIEW and EMPATHY on the whiteboard.
notes.ask: Which word means caring about how someone else feels?
notes.listen: Empathy. Pathways asks her to TYPE point of view, perspective, empathy and interpret, so have her spell empathy and perspective out loud.

slides.title: Same moment, two views
slides.text:
Point of view is the way one person sees a moment.
It is like a camera. Each person has their own camera.
Two people can see the same moment in two ways.

visual.text:
🧑 Theo: “He is rude.”
👧 Mia: “He is exhausted.”
Same moment, two points of view.

steps.text: The moment: the hiker left and did not buy anything.
Theo's view: he felt hurt. He thought the hiker was rude.
Mia's view: she saw clues. She thought the hiker was exhausted.
What a person notices and feels shapes their point of view.

slides.tip: A different point of view is not automatically wrong. It is just a different angle.

notes.do: Reveal one step at a time. Hold up the THEO card, then the MIA card.
notes.say: Point of view is like a camera angle. Theo's camera saw a man leave. Mia's camera zoomed in on his boots, his pack and his bottle.
notes.ask: What moment did Theo and Mia see in two different ways?
notes.listen: The hiker left without buying anything. Pathways asks about this moment as a typed question, so have her say the whole thing.

slides.title: Clues help you infer
slides.text:
The story never says the hiker was tired.
Mia used clues. She inferred it.
To infer is to figure something out from clues.

visual.text:
🥾 muddy boots + 🎒 torn strap + 🧴 empty bottle
➡️ The hiker is exhausted, not rude.

steps.text: Clue 1: his boots were caked in mud. He walked a long way.
Clue 2: the strap on his pack was torn. It was a rough hike.
Clue 3: his water bottle was empty. He was thirsty.
Clues + what you know = an inference. It is not a wild guess.

slides.tip: Ask: What clue makes me think that?

notes.do: Reveal one clue at a time. She points to each clue in the story on the previous slide if she needs it.
notes.say: You learned the word infer in Lesson 1. Mia did not guess. She used real clues.
notes.ask: Which clue do you think is the strongest? Why?
notes.listen: Any clue with a reason (the empty bottle means he ran out of water on the trail). If she says 'he was sad', ask: which clue tells you that?

slides.title: Theo's view or Mia's view?
slides.text: Who would say this? Tap a card. Then tap a box.

items.text: “That hiker was rude!”
items.hint: Who felt hurt when the hiker left?

items.text: “His boots are caked in mud.”
items.hint: Who looked closer at the hiker?

items.text: “My feelings are hurt.”
items.why: Theo felt hurt when the hiker left.

items.text: “The strap on his pack is torn.”
“He is not rude. He is exhausted.”
“His water bottle is empty.”

slides.done: Theo saw a man leave. Mia saw the clues. Same moment, two points of view.

notes.do: She reads each card aloud in the voice of the person who would say it.
notes.ask: Why did Theo not notice the boots?
notes.listen: He was busy feeling hurt (any reasonable answer). Then say: our feelings can change what we notice.

slides.title: Both views are real
slides.text:
Mia told Theo about the clues.
Theo's hurt feelings were real.
Mia's idea was probably true too.
Put both views together. You get a fuller understanding.

visual.sub: Theo's view + Mia's view = the whole picture

steps.text: Ask: What does each person notice?
Ask: How does each person feel?
You do not have to pick a winner. Both can be true.
Caring about how someone else feels is empathy.

slides.tip: Fuller means more complete. You see more of the picture.

notes.do: Put the THEO and MIA cards side by side, touching.
notes.say: Theo was not wrong to feel hurt. Mia was not wrong either. Together they see the whole picture.
notes.ask: How did Mia show empathy for the hiker?
notes.listen: She thought about how tired and thirsty he was instead of being upset. Pathways asks her to type fuller and empathy.

slides.title: A rainy Saturday
slides.text: Read this new story. Then answer.

visual.text:
Rain fell all day Saturday. Kiko's soccer game was called off. She sat by the window and sighed.
Her grandpa grinned at the rain. “My tomato plants were so dry!” he said.

items.q: How did Kiko feel about the rain? Type one word.
items.why: Her game was called off and she sighed. She felt sad or disappointed.
items.no: Look at the clues: no game, and she sighed.

items.q: Why was Grandpa happy about the rain?
choices: He wanted to stay inside all day.
items.why: His tomato plants were dry. Rain gives them water.
no: Kiko's game was called off, not Grandpa's.
The story does not say that.

items.q: Can both points of view be true at the same time? Type yes or no.
items.why: Yes. Kiko is sad, and Grandpa is glad. Both feelings are real.
items.no: Kiko's feeling is real. Is Grandpa's feeling real too?

notes.do: She reads it aloud. On the whiteboard, draw two faces: KIKO and GRANDPA. She writes one feeling and one clue under each.
notes.ask: Same rain. Why do they feel so differently?
notes.listen: Sad (or disappointed), his plants needed water, yes. Kiko cared about soccer, Grandpa cared about his plants.

slides.title: Reading check
slides.text: On your own. No looking back!

items.q: Theo's point of view: the hiker was being ____.
items.why: Theo thought the hiker was being rude.
items.no: Theo felt hurt. He thought the hiker was being r…

items.q: Which clue did Mia notice?
choices: a big smile on his face
a torn strap on his pack
a new map in his hand
a shiny new hat on his head
items.why: Mia saw the torn strap, the muddy boots and the empty water bottle.
no: The story does not say he smiled.
The story does not say he had a map.
The story does not say he had a hat.

items.q: Mia's point of view: the hiker was not rude. He was ____.
items.why: Mia inferred the hiker was exhausted, not rude.
items.no: Think of the empty bottle and the muddy boots. He was very, very tired.

items.q: Understanding and caring about how someone else feels is called ____.
items.no: It starts with em.

notes.do: On her own. Note her first answers.
notes.listen: Rude, a torn strap, exhausted (tired is OK here, but Pathways wants exhausted), empathy. Watch the spelling of exhausted and empathy.

slides.title: Math words
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Read the word. Then spell price and factor out loud.

words.meaning: To count by a number that is not 1.
A number you land on when you skip-count.

notes.do: Flip each card. She reads it. Then she spells price and factor out loud while you write them on the whiteboard. Pathways asks her to TYPE price, multiple, factor and total.
notes.ask: In 4 × 10 = 40, which numbers are the factors?
notes.listen: 4 and 10. If she says 40, say: 40 is the product, the answer. Factors are the numbers we multiply.

slides.title: Skip-count by 5s and 10s
slides.text:
When you skip-count, you jump by the same number each time.
Every number you land on is a multiple.

steps.text: That is 9 jumps of 5. So 9 × 5 = 45.
Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. Multiples of 10 end in 0.

slides.tip: The number of jumps tells you the factor. Where you land is the answer.

notes.do: Hands-on first: she lays down nine $5 slips one at a time and says the total each time: 5, 10, 15 … 45. Then six $10 slips: 10, 20 … 60.
notes.say: Skip-counting and times facts are the same skill. The 9th jump by 5 lands on 45, and 9 × 5 = 45.
notes.ask: Is 72 a multiple of 5? How do you know?
notes.listen: No, it ends in 2. Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5.

slides.title: Skip-count
slides.text: Use your money slips if it helps.

items.q: Skip-count by 5s: 55, 60, 65, ____
items.no: Add 5 to the last number.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 10?
items.why: Multiples of 10 end in 0. 90 is 9 jumps of 10.
no: 35 ends in 5. It is a multiple of 5, not 10.
54 does not end in 0.
101 ends in 1, not 0.

items.q: How many jumps of 10 does it take to get to 70?
items.no: Count by 10s and hold up a finger for each jump.
Add 10 to the last number.

notes.do: She says each skip-count out loud and touches a slip for each jump.
notes.listen: 70, 90, 7, 90. If she says 75 for 55, 60, 65 …, she added 10: point to the jumps of 5.

slides.title: Price × quantity = total
slides.text:
Grandpa sells bags of nuts for $5 each.
A hiker buys 8 bags. How much is that?

steps.text: Find the price of one: $5.
Find the quantity, how many: 8 bags.
Multiply: 5 × 8 = 40.
Check by skip-counting 8 jumps: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. The total is $40.

slides.tip: Clue words each, per and every often mean multiply.

notes.do: She writes a price tag on an index card: NUTS $5 EACH. Then she counts out eight $5 slips and skip-counts them.
notes.say: The full amount is the total. You learned total in Lesson 4. Price times quantity equals the total.
notes.ask: What would 8 bags cost if the price were $10 each?
notes.listen: $80. If she says $18, she added: ask, are there 8 equal groups of $10?

slides.title: Multiply, or add or subtract?
slides.text: Read each problem. Do you multiply? Or do you add or subtract? Tap a card. Then tap a box.

items.text: Bird feeders cost $5 each. Ines buys 6. How much?
Otis had $40. He spent $10. How much is left?
items.hint: Is it equal groups, or is money taken away?

items.text: Pens cost $10 per box. Mom buys 3 boxes. How much?
A hat costs $10. A scarf costs $5. How much for both?
Every bag of rice costs $5. Pearl buys 7 bags. How much?
Quinn has $25. Esther has $30. How much more does Esther have?
items.hint: Is anything repeated in equal groups?

slides.done: Same price, many items: multiply. Different prices or money taken away: add or subtract.

notes.do: She reads each problem aloud and circles the clue word on the whiteboard before she taps.
notes.ask: In the hat and scarf problem, why can't you multiply?
notes.listen: The prices are not the same, so there are no equal groups. If she multiplies 10 × 5, ask: is it 5 hats at $10?

slides.title: Price tags
slides.text: Find the price. Find the quantity. Then multiply.

items.q: Wool socks cost $5 a pair. A hiker buys 6 pairs. What is the total?
items.no: Skip-count by 5s, 6 jumps.

items.q: Flashlights cost $10 each. A camp buys 7. What is the total?
items.no: Skip-count by 10s, 7 jumps.

items.q: Lamps cost $10 each. Mabel buys 3. Which number sentence finds the total?
items.why: Same price for each lamp, 3 lamps: 10 × 3 = 30. The total is $30.
no: That adds the price and the quantity. 3 lamps at $10 each are 3 equal groups.
Nothing is taken away.

items.q: In $10 × 4 = $40, the $40 is the full amount. It is called the ____.
items.no: It is the full amount. It starts with t.

notes.do: For each one she writes the price tag on an index card, then counts out the money slips.
notes.listen: $30, $70, 10 × 3, total. If she adds (5 + 6 = 11), say: 6 pairs, and each pair costs $5. Lay down a $5 slip for each pair.

slides.title: Math check
slides.text: On your own. Skip-count on paper if you need to.

items.q: Skip-count by 5s: 75, 80, 85, ____
items.no: Add 5 to the last number.

items.q: Bug spray costs $5 a can. Grandpa buys 9 cans. What is the total?
items.no: Skip-count by 5s, 9 jumps.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 5?
items.why: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. 65 ends in 5.
no: 47 ends in 7.
53 ends in 3.
58 ends in 8.

items.q: In 8 × 5 = 40, which numbers are the factors?
items.why: Factors are the numbers you multiply: 8 and 5. The 40 is the product.
no: 40 is the answer, the product. It is not a factor.
40 is the answer, the product. It is not a factor.

notes.do: On her own. Note her first answers.
notes.listen: 90, $45, 65, 8 and 5. If she picks 47 or 53, remind her: multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. If she picks 40 as a factor, say: 40 is the answer, the product.

slides.title: Two big skills
slides.text:
Reading: two people can see one moment in two ways. Look for clues.
Math: skip-count by 5s and 10s. Price × quantity = total.
slides.tip: Friday is New Year's Day. No work that day! Read your list with Mr. Jonathan.

notes.do: Open the course page. Read the task list with her, one line at a time. Hand her the printed packet.
notes.say: Great start to the new year. Your next lesson is next Tuesday.
notes.ask: Tell me one time you and someone else saw the same thing in two different ways.
notes.listen: Any real example, with how each person felt.

slides.title: On Your Own: Views and Prices
slides.text: You learned two big skills in class. Now try them on your own. Take your time. 👀🏷️

slides.title: Explain it out loud
slides.text: Say these to a grown-up, or say them out loud to yourself.
prompts: Why did Theo and Mia see the hiker in two different ways?
How do you find the total when every item costs $5?

slides.title: Your 9 words
slides.text: Tap each card. Say the word. Say what it means.

words.meaning: The way one person sees a moment.
words.example: From Theo's point of view, the hiker was rude.

words.meaning: A person's own way of seeing or understanding something.
Understanding and caring about how someone else feels.
words.example: Mia showed empathy for the tired hiker.

words.meaning: To explain what something means to you.
words.example: Theo and Mia interpreted the same moment in two ways.

words.meaning: To count by a number that is not 1.
A number you land on when you skip-count.

slides.title: Two points of view
slides.text:
Two people can see the same moment in two ways.
What each person notices and feels shapes their view.
Use clues to infer what someone feels.

visual.text:
🧑 Theo felt hurt.
👧 Mia saw the clues.
Both views can be true.

slides.tip: Ask: What clue makes me think that?

slides.title: A chewed sneaker
slides.text: Read the story. Then answer.

visual.text:
Nora and her brother Felix made a paper boat. They put it in the pond. It sank.
Felix groaned. “All that work!”
Nora giggled. “Now the fish have a boat!”

items.q: How did Felix feel? Type one word.
items.why: Felix groaned about all his work. He felt upset.
items.no: Look at the clue: he groaned.

items.q: How did Nora feel?
choices: She was scared of the pond.
items.why: Nora giggled. She thought it was funny.
no: The story does not say she was mad.
She giggled. That is not scared.

items.q: Felix and Nora saw the same moment in two ways. They had two points of ____.
items.no: Points of v…

slides.title: Is Oscar cold?
slides.text: Which details are clues that Oscar is cold? Tap a card. Then tap a box.

items.text: His teeth are chattering.
items.hint: Does this happen when you are cold?

items.text: He has a red backpack.
items.why: A backpack does not tell how he feels.
items.hint: Does this tell you anything about cold?

items.text: He rubs his hands together.
items.why: People rub their hands to warm them.
items.hint: Why do people rub their hands?

items.text: His sister's name is Hazel.
items.why: A name is not a clue about cold.
items.hint: Does a name tell you he is cold?

items.text: He zips his coat up to his chin.
items.hint: Why would he zip his coat so high?

items.text: He likes math class.
items.why: Liking math does not tell you he is cold.

slides.done: Good readers use the clues that matter. That is how you infer.

slides.title: Infer it
slides.text: Read. Use the clues.

visual.text: Joel came in from the yard. His knees had green grass stains. He held a muddy ball. His face was red and sweaty. He was grinning.

items.q: What can you infer about Joel?
choices: He was sleeping in his bed.
items.why: Grass stains, a muddy ball and a sweaty face are clues. He was playing outside.
no: Sleeping would not give him grass stains.
Reading would not make him sweaty.

items.q: To figure something out from clues is to ____.
items.why: To figure something out from clues is to infer.
items.no: It starts with in. Mia did it in the hiker story.

items.q: Was Joel happy or sad? Type happy or sad.
items.why: He was grinning. That is a clue that he was happy.
items.no: Look at the last sentence. What was his face doing?

slides.title: Skip-count and multiply
slides.text:
Skip-count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 …
Skip-count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 …
Price × quantity = total.
slides.tip: Each, per and every are clues to multiply.

items.q: Skip-count by 5s: 60, 65, 70, ____
items.no: Add 5 to the last number.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 10?
items.why: Multiples of 10 end in 0. 85 ends in 5. It is a multiple of 5, not 10.
no: 30 ends in 0. It is 3 jumps of 10.
70 ends in 0. It is 7 jumps of 10.
100 ends in 0. It is 10 jumps of 10.

items.q: Skip-count by 10s: 40, 50, 60, ____
items.no: Add 10 to the last number.

items.q: How many jumps of 5 does it take to get to 35?
items.no: Count by 5s. Hold up a finger for each jump.

slides.title: Price problems
slides.text: Find the price. Find the quantity. Multiply.

items.q: Whistles cost $5 each. Tariq buys 7. What is the total?
items.no: Skip-count by 5s, 7 jumps.

items.q: Tin cups cost $10 each. A troop buys 9. What is the total?
items.no: Skip-count by 10s, 9 jumps.

items.q: Esme says 4 bags at $5 each cost $9. What did she do wrong?
items.why: 4 + 5 = 9. She should multiply: 4 × 5 = 20. The total is $20.
no: By 10s, 4 jumps land on 40, not 9.
3 bags would cost $15, not $9.

slides.title: Multiply, add or subtract?
slides.text: Read carefully. Not every problem is a times problem!

items.q: Bandanas cost $5 each. Sadie buys 8. What is the total?
items.why: Same price, 8 items: 8 × 5 = 40. The total is $40.
items.no: Each bandana is $5. Skip-count by 5s, 8 jumps.

items.q: Uma has $50. She spends $10. How much is left? What do you do?
no: There are no equal groups here.
She spends money, so she has less, not more.

items.q: Toby buys a $10 kite and a $5 ball. How much does he spend in all?
items.no: The prices are not the same. Add them.

items.q: Which one is true?
items.why: Both have 5 hundreds. 531 has 3 tens. 513 has 1 ten. So 531 > 513.
no: 531 has 3 tens and 513 has 1 ten. 531 is bigger.
The digits are in a different order, so they are not equal.

items.why: You can't take 6 from 2, and there are 0 tens. Regroup a hundred into 10 tens, then a ten into 10 ones. 12 − 6 = 6. 9 − 9 = 0. 6 − 2 = 4. 406.
items.no: There are 0 tens. Regroup from the hundreds first.

items.q: The problem in a story is called the ____.
items.why: The problem in a story is the conflict.
items.no: It starts with con.

sets.q: Skip-count by 5s: 70, 75, 80, ____
Mia skip-counts by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 21, 25. Which number is a mistake?
sets.why: 15 + 5 = 20, not 21. Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5.
no: 10 is right. 5 + 5 = 10.

sets.q: Postcards cost $5 each. Vera buys 10. What is the total?
In 6 × 10 = 60, the 6 and the 10 are called ____.
sets.why: Numbers you multiply are factors.
sets.no: They are the numbers you multiply. It starts with f.

sets.q: The way one person sees a moment is their point of ____.
sets.why: That is their point of view.

sets.q: What can you infer about Lucia?
sets.why: Yawning and closing eyes are clues. She is sleepy.
no: An excited person would not put her head down.
No clue is about food.

visual.text: Lucia yawned. Her eyes kept closing. She put her head down on her desk.

sets.q: How did Iris feel about the drill?
choices: glad she learned the way out
angry that the drill was so long
sets.why: Iris clapped and said she knew the way out. She was glad.
no: That was Ezra's point of view, not Iris's.
The story does not say the drill was long.

visual.text:
The school had a fire drill. The bell was very loud. Little Ezra cried and covered his ears.
His big sister Iris clapped. “Now I know the way out!” she said.

sets.q: In The Grumpy Hiker, the strap on the hiker's pack was ____.
sets.why: The strap was torn. It was a clue that he had a rough hike.
sets.no: Mia saw the strap. It was not whole.

sets.q: Skip-count by 10s: 60, 70, 80, ____
Which number is a multiple of 5?
sets.why: Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. 45 ends in 5.
no: 41 ends in 1.
52 ends in 2.
54 ends in 4.

sets.q: Walking sticks cost $10 each. A shop orders 8. What is the total?
The number on a price tag tells how much one thing costs. That number is the ____.
sets.why: How much one thing costs is its price.
sets.no: It goes on a price tag. It starts with p.

sets.q: Dina's friend was sad. Dina thought about how her friend felt and sat with her. Dina showed ____.
sets.why: Caring about how someone else feels is empathy.
sets.no: It is one of your reading words. It starts with em.

sets.q: What can you infer about the weather?
choices: It is a hot, sunny day.
sets.why: A wet shirt, dripping hair and an umbrella are clues. It is raining.
no: Juice would not make his hair drip, and it does not explain the umbrella.
A sunny day would not need an umbrella.

visual.text: Reggie came inside. His shirt was wet. His hair dripped on the floor. He shook a wet umbrella.

sets.q: How did Gwen feel about the snake?
sets.why: Gwen stepped back and held her breath. She was nervous.
no: That was Kenji's point of view.
Stepping back is not a clue for bored.

visual.text:
The class got a pet snake. Kenji's eyes lit up. He ran to the tank.
Gwen stepped back and held her breath.

sets.q: In The Grumpy Hiker, Theo felt ____ when the hiker left.
sets.why: Theo felt hurt. He thought the hiker was rude.

sets.q: Skip-count by 5s: 85, 90, 95, ____
Theo skip-counts by 10s: 30, 45, 50, 60, 70. Which number is a mistake?

teacher.objective: Ce'Line compares two characters' points of view on the same moment in The Grumpy Hiker: Theo felt hurt and thought the hiker was rude; Mia noticed the muddy boots, the torn strap and the empty water bottle and inferred he was exhausted. She explains that both views can be real, uses clues to infer how a character feels in new stories, and types the Week 7 words (point of view, perspective, empathy, interpret). In math she skip-counts by 5s and 10s (up to 100), knows that multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5 and multiples of 10 end in 0, connects the number of jumps to a times fact (9 jumps of 5 = 9 × 5 = 45), and solves pricing word problems with price × quantity = total, choosing multiply only when every item has the same price.
materials: The class lesson on a laptop or tablet (teacher code 9110)
20 paper money slips cut from index cards: 10 say $5 and 10 say $10
8 index cards: 2 that say THEO and MIA, 6 blank for price tags
Whiteboard and two marker colors, pencil
Her Lesson 6 Packet page 2 (she brings it) and the new Packet (2 pages), printed for her to take home: page 1 is math, page 2 is reading

plan.do: Class slide 1. Warm hello and one thing about her break. Glance at her Lesson 6 packet and Pathways Week 6 scores.
Class slide 2. Round 817, 388 + 484 = 872, estimate 63 + 79 = 140, 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 = 5 × 7, the icy road. She says each answer before she types.
Class slide 3. Take turns reading The Grumpy Hiker aloud. THEO card left, MIA card right. Check she knows exhausted.
Class slide 4. Four cards: point of view, perspective, empathy, interpret. She spells empathy and perspective out loud.
Class slide 5. Point of view is a camera angle. She says which moment they saw in two ways.
Class slide 6. Mud, torn strap, empty bottle → exhausted. Ask: which clue makes you think that?
Class slide 7. She reads each card in that person's voice, then sorts.
Class slide 8. THEO and MIA cards side by side. Fuller understanding, empathy.
Class slide 9. Two faces on the whiteboard: one feeling and one clue for Kiko and for Grandpa.
Class slide 10 on her own: rude, a torn strap, exhausted, empathy.
Class slide 11. Five cards. She spells price and factor out loud.
Class slide 12. She lays down nine $5 slips (5 … 45), then six $10 slips (10 … 60). Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5.
Class slide 13. She touches a slip for each jump: 70, 90, 7 jumps, 90.
Class slide 14. She writes a NUTS $5 EACH price tag and counts out eight $5 slips: $40.

plan.block: 4:47 · Sort: multiply, or add or subtract?
plan.do: Class slide 15. She circles the clue word on the whiteboard before she taps.
Class slide 16. Price tag card, then money slips: $30, $70, 10 × 3, total.
Class slide 17 on her own: 90, $45, 65, 8 and 5. Note her first answers.
Class slide 18. Read the task list with her one line at a time (no work Friday, New Year's Day). Hand her the printed packet.

watch: Theo vs. Mia: Pathways asks who felt hurt (Theo), who noticed the clues (Mia), what Theo thought the hiker was (rude) and what Mia inferred (exhausted). Say: Theo felt it, Mia saw it.
'Theo was wrong': Pathways wants 'his hurt feelings were still real'. If she says Theo was wrong, ask: did Theo really feel hurt? Then both views are real.
Inferring vs. guessing: every feeling she names must come with a clue from the story. If she says 'he was sad', ask: which clue tells you that?
Whose view? In the new stories (Kiko and Grandpa), she may give the same feeling to both people. Ask: what does EACH person care about?
Spelling: exhausted, empathy, perspective and interpret are typed in Pathways. Watch for exausted, empethy, prespective.
Adding the price and the quantity: $5 and 6 pairs → 11 means she added. Lay down one $5 slip for each pair and skip-count.
Skip-count slips: if she adds 10 when counting by 5s (55, 60, 65, 75), have her touch one slip per jump and say each number.
Spot the mistake: in a skip-count list, check every jump. By 5s, every number ends in 0 or 5. By 10s, every number ends in 0. 21 or 45 in the wrong list is the mistake.
Multiples: multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5; multiples of 10 end in 0. 35 is a multiple of 5 but not of 10.
Not every money problem is multiply: 'left' and 'how much more' mean subtract; two different prices mean add. Same price for each item means multiply.

packet_key.answer: 40 − 10 = 30; $30 is left. Subtract, because she spent money (it was taken away); there are no equal groups.
point of view → the way one person sees a moment
perspective → a person's own way of seeing things
empathy → caring about how someone else feels
interpret → to explain what something means to you
Emil felt happy (or calm, ready). Clue: he smiled, and he had studied all week.
Fern felt nervous (or worried, scared). Clue: her stomach flipped, and she forgot to study.
Answers vary: one real moment, how she felt and how the other person felt, in full sentences.

teacher.notes: For you only: this lesson is one Pathways week (Week 7: Pricing Day at the Trading Post and The Grumpy Hiker). The math is skip-counting by 5s and 10s (to 100), multiples, and pricing word problems (price × quantity = total) with $5 and $10 prices, plus the words skip-count, multiple, factor, price and total; quantity is added because it names the second factor. The reading skill is point of view: comparing Theo's and Mia's views of the same moment and inferring from clues. Infer and total were taught in Lessons 1 and 4, so they are reviewed, not new vocabulary cards. The class lesson uses the real hiker story because Pathways Week 7 Reading asks about it; the after-class lesson, Practice and Show What You Know use new KCE stories and new numbers. Show What You Know has 8 questions (4 math, 4 reading; 3 different sets for retakes; she needs 85, so 7 of 8). This week: the task list runs Tue, Dec 29 to Mon, Jan 4, with Friday (New Year's Day) free: after-class lesson Tuesday, Practice Wednesday, Packet page 1 Thursday, Pathways Week 7 Reading Saturday, Packet page 2 and Practice again Sunday, Pathways Week 7 Math Monday. Both Pathways lessons ask for a printed Pre/Post sheet; print it for her today if she has no printer at home. If a Pathways Week 6 lesson is still under 85, add it to her Wednesday (after Practice); the Week 7 warm-up already reviews equal groups and cause and effect. Science Week 7 and Social Studies Week 7 are optional and not taught. Next lesson: Tue, Jan 5. Start it by checking her packet and her Pathways Week 7 scores. If she is under 85 on Show What You Know, open the Formspree missed list: a missed skip-count or multiple item means 5 minutes with the money slips (touch one per jump); a missed price problem means writing the price tag first, then price × quantity; a missed point-of-view item means the THEO and MIA cards (who felt it, who saw it); a missed infer item means 'which clue makes you think that?' with a new short story. If either Pathways Week 7 lesson is under 85, she retakes it with you at the start of that lesson.
